insight.title: Why Solving One Problem Always Creates a New One
insight.subtitle: Why you should stop expecting your business to eventually run itself

sections.text: We often treat business challenges like a checklist. We think that if we just hire that person or fix that software, we’ll finally be "done." But in biology, the "Red Queen" rule applies.

Evolutionary biology shows that species must constantly change just to maintain their current position. In business, your "solutions" don't end the race; they simply change the nature of the competition you are facing.

Stop waiting for the moment when everything is finally "under control." Effective strategy accepts that every upgrade shifts the pressure elsewhere. Your goal isn't to eliminate friction, but to choose which friction matters.
Try this today: When you finish a task today, identify the new bottleneck that your success just created.
Progress is not the absence of problems, but the presence of better ones.
